title: Perimeter and area of polygons
blurb: Tell perimeter from area, apply the rectangle, triangle, parallelogram and trapezoid formulas, and price composite floors in square feet or square yards.
question: A clinic waiting room is 15 ft by 12 ft, and carpet is sold by the square yard at $27 per square yard. How much will the carpet cost?

teach.h: Around the edge, or the space inside
teach.body: Formally, the perimeter of a polygon is the sum of the lengths of its sides, measured in linear units (ft, m); its area is the number of unit squares that cover the region, measured in square units (ft², m²). In plain English: perimeter is the fence around a yard, area is the grass inside it. Before you calculate anything, decide which one the question is asking for.

teach.caption: A square of side s: P = 4s and A = s².

head: Shape
Area
Watch out
rows: Same units for l and w
h is not the slanted side
teach.caption: A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height; that is where the 1/2 comes from.

teach.body: In every area formula, the height h is the straight-up distance measured at a right angle (90°) to the base. A slanted side is NOT the height, even if it is the only other length you can see in the figure. When a question gives both a slanted side and a height, the slanted side is there to tempt you; it is used only for perimeter.

items: Triangle, base 10 cm, height 6 cm: A = 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². Check: a 10 × 6 rectangle is 60 cm², and half is 30.
Parallelogram, base 9 m, height 4 m, slanted side 5 m: A = 9 × 4 = 36 m². The 5 m side gives the perimeter: 2(9 + 5) = 28 m.
Trapezoid, bases 8 in and 12 in, height 5 in: A = 1/2 × (8 + 12) × 5 = 1/2 × 20 × 5 = 50 in². Check: average base 10 × 5 = 50.
Room 12 ft × 15 ft, carpet $3.50 per ft²: A = 180 ft², and 180 × 3.50 = $630. Check: 630 ÷ 3.50 = 180.

teach.h: Two ways to handle a composite figure

root.label: Composite figure
root.sub: Split it into shapes you know

teach.caption: Sketch the figure, label every length, and keep all lengths in the same unit before you multiply.

teach.h: Scenario: Carlos prices an L-shaped room
teach.body: Carlos, a nursing applicant working weekends for a flooring company, measures an L-shaped room: a 20 ft by 15 ft rectangle with an 8 ft by 6 ft corner missing. Area: 20 × 15 = 300 ft², minus 8 × 6 = 48 ft², gives 252 ft². Carpet at $3.50 per ft² costs 252 × 3.50 = $882. For baseboard trim, he needs the perimeter: cutting a corner notch keeps it the same as the full rectangle, 2(20 + 15) = 70 ft.

teach.h: Why 1 square yard is 9 square feet
teach.caption: 1 yd = 3 ft, so 1 yd² = 3 × 3 = 9 ft². Likewise 1 ft² = 12 × 12 = 144 in², and 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm².

teach.text: Square units square the factor. 1 yd² is 9 ft² (not 3), and 1 ft² is 144 in² (not 12). Other classic slips: answering with the perimeter when the area was asked, forgetting the 1/2 for triangles and trapezoids, and using a slanted side as the height.

items: Perimeter = sum of the sides (linear units). Area = space covered (square units).
Rectangle lw; square s²; triangle 1/2 bh; parallelogram bh; trapezoid 1/2(b1 + b2)h.
Height is perpendicular to the base; a slanted side is not the height.
Composite figures: add joined pieces, subtract cut-outs.
1 ft² = 144 in²; 1 yd² = 9 ft²; 1 m² = 10,000 cm². Convert lengths first if units differ.

summary: You can now decide whether a problem needs perimeter or area and apply the right formula for rectangles, squares, triangles, parallelograms and trapezoids. You can also split composite figures and convert square units correctly before pricing a job.

A.q: A rectangular garden is 18 ft long and 12 ft wide. Fencing costs $4.25 per foot. How much will it cost to fence all four sides?
A.why: Fencing goes around the edge, so find the perimeter: 2(18) + 2(12) = 60 ft. 60 × $4.25 = $255.00. Check: 255 ÷ 4.25 = 60.

whyNot.0: This uses the area (18 × 12 = 216 ft²) instead of the perimeter.
whyNot.2: This adds only one length and one width (30 ft); a rectangle has four sides.
whyNot.3: This fences only the two long sides (36 ft).

A.q: A triangle has a base of 14 cm, a height of 9 cm and a slanted side of 11 cm. What is its area?
A.why: A = 1/2 × b × h = 1/2 × 14 × 9 = 63 cm². The 11 cm side is not perpendicular to the base, so it is not used.

whyNot.1: This uses the slanted side as the height: 1/2 × 14 × 11 = 77.
whyNot.2: This multiplies the base by the slanted side and forgets the 1/2.

A.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 10 in and 16 in and a height of 7 in. What is its area?

whyNot.2: This uses only the longer base: 16 × 7 = 112.
whyNot.3: This uses only the shorter base: 10 × 7 = 70.

B.q: A square patio has a perimeter of 48 ft. What is its area?
B.why: A square has 4 equal sides: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 ft. Area = 12 × 12 = 144 ft².

whyNot.0: This squares the perimeter (48 × 48) instead of the side.
whyNot.1: This divides the perimeter by 2 to get a side of 24 ft; a square has 4 sides.
whyNot.3: This multiplies the perimeter by 4 instead of dividing.

B.q: A bulletin board is 3 ft wide and 4 ft tall. What is its area in square inches?
B.why: Convert the lengths first: 36 in × 48 in = 1,728 in². Check: 3 × 4 = 12 ft², and 12 × 144 = 1,728 in².

whyNot.0: This multiplies 12 ft² by 12, the linear factor; each square foot is 144 in².
whyNot.2: This is the perimeter in inches: 2(36) + 2(48) = 168.
whyNot.3: This multiplies 12 ft² by 1,728, the cubic-inch factor.

B.q: A parallelogram has a base of 15 m, a slanted side of 8 m and a height of 6 m. What is its area?
B.why: A = b × h = 15 × 6 = 90 m². The slanted side is used only for the perimeter.

whyNot.0: This multiplies the base by the slanted side (15 × 8).
whyNot.1: This uses the triangle formula: 1/2 × 15 × 6. A parallelogram has no 1/2.
whyNot.2: This is the perimeter, 2(15 + 8) = 46 m, not the area.

C.q: A rectangular lawn is 40 ft by 25 ft. A 12 ft by 10 ft patio sits in one corner. Sod for the rest of the lawn costs $0.80 per square foot. What is the cost of the sod?

whyNot.1: This sods the whole rectangle (1,000 × 0.80) without subtracting the patio.
whyNot.2: This adds the patio area instead of subtracting it (1,120 × 0.80).
whyNot.3: This prices only the patio area (120 × 0.80).

C.q: A clinic waiting room is 15 ft by 12 ft. Carpet is sold by the square yard at $27 per square yard. What is the cost of carpeting the room?
C.why: Area 15 × 12 = 180 ft². 1 yd² = 9 ft², so 180 ÷ 9 = 20 yd². 20 × $27 = $540. Check: 5 yd × 4 yd = 20 yd².

whyNot.0: This divides by 3 (the linear factor) instead of 9 (180 ÷ 3 = 60 yd²).
whyNot.1: This multiplies square feet by the price per square yard without converting.
whyNot.3: This uses the perimeter (54 ft = 18 yd) instead of the area.

C.q: The front wall of a house is a rectangle 24 ft wide and 10 ft tall, topped by a triangular gable with the same 24 ft base and a height of 6 ft. What is the total area of the wall?
C.why: Rectangle: 24 × 10 = 240 ft². Triangle: 1/2 × 24 × 6 = 72 ft². Total: 240 + 72 = 312 ft².

whyNot.0: This forgets the 1/2 for the triangle (240 + 144).
whyNot.2: This halves the base to 12 ft and then applies the 1/2 as well (1/2 × 12 × 6 = 36), halving twice.
whyNot.3: This includes only the rectangle and leaves out the gable.

reteach.title: Think of framing and filling a picture
reteach.question: A picture frame goes around a photo, and the glass covers it. Which one is perimeter and which one is area?

blocks.body: The frame is a strip that runs around the edge: you buy it by length, so it is perimeter. The glass covers the whole photo: you buy it by surface, so it is area. An 8 in by 10 in photo needs 2(8) + 2(10) = 36 in of frame, but 8 × 10 = 80 in² of glass. Same photo, different question, different units.

blocks.text: Check the unit in the answer choices: plain units (ft) mean perimeter; square units (ft²) mean area. A number with the wrong kind of unit is a trap.

explain.body: Add every side. For a rectangle, P = 2l + 2w. If one side is described in terms of another (3 times as long), find each length first.

test.q: A rectangular dog run is 3 times as long as it is wide. The width is 7 ft. What is the perimeter?

whyNot.0: This adds one length and one width (21 + 7); a rectangle has four sides.
whyNot.1: This is the area (21 × 7), not the perimeter.
whyNot.2: This counts only the two long sides.

explain.body: A = l × w for a rectangle and A = b × h for a parallelogram. Given the area and one side, divide to find the other: w = A ÷ l.

test.q: A rectangular room has an area of 96 m² and a length of 12 m. What is its width?

whyNot.2: This subtracts the length from the area.

explain.body: Both formulas have a 1/2: A = 1/2 bh and A = 1/2(b1 + b2)h. Working backward for a triangle's height: h = 2A ÷ b.

test.q: A triangular sail has an area of 54 ft² and a base of 12 ft. What is its height?

whyNot.0: This divides 54 by 12 and forgets to double: that ignores the 1/2 in the formula.
whyNot.1: This subtracts the base from the area.
whyNot.3: This multiplies the area by the base instead of dividing.

explain.body: A square unit converts by the SQUARE of the length factor: 1 yd² = 3 × 3 = 9 ft², 1 ft² = 12 × 12 = 144 in².

test.q: How many square feet are in 5 square yards?

whyNot.0: This uses the linear factor 3; a square yard is 3 ft × 3 ft = 9 ft².
whyNot.2: This uses 27, the cubic factor (1 yd³ = 27 ft³).
whyNot.3: This divides by 9 instead of multiplying.
